1. `rule/struct_tag.go`, `Configure()` — the "disabled" directive is only recognized when `len(parts) == 2`. Any other arrangement (e.g. `"validate,disabled,extra"`, or "disabled" appearing with another option for the same key) silently falls through to the normal option-parsing loop and gets stored as a literal custom option string `"disabled"` instead of erroring or disabling. This is a confusing, undocumented edge case for a brand-new public config keyword. Fix: detect `"disabled"` anywhere in `parts[1:]` and either treat the whole entry as a disable-directive consistently or return a config error when it's combined with other options, instead of silently misinterpreting it.

2. `rule/struct_tag.go`, `checkTaggedField()` — `tagKey := tagKey(tag.Key)` shadows the package-level type `tagKey` with a local variable of the same name. This hurts readability and is a landmine for future edits in that scope (any reference to the `tagKey` type there now resolves to the variable). Rename the local variable (e.g. `key`), consistent with how `Configure()` already names its equivalent variable.

3. `testdata/struct_tag_disabled_checkers.go` — file has no trailing newline and contains trailing whitespace on several lines (after the `Field8`/`Field9` comments). `gofmt`/`golangci-lint` will flag this and likely break CI. Run `gofmt -w` on all changed files before merge (also check `rule/struct_tag.go` for the stray blank line with a trailing tab introduced around `r.disabledCheckers = make(...)`).

4. `test/struct_tag_test.go` — the new test only exercises the happy path (two independently-disabled keys) through the golden-file fixture. There's no coverage for the Configure-level edge cases this PR introduces: combining `"key,disabled"` with custom options for the same key, malformed combinations like `"validate,disabled,extra"`, or case sensitivity of the `disabled` keyword. Add direct unit tests against `Configure()`'s error/parsing behavior, not just an end-to-end lint fixture.

5. Design/API scope — overloading the existing comma-separated "custom options" argument syntax with a magic string `"disabled"` mixes two distinct concerns (per-checker custom options vs. an enable/disable toggle) into one ambiguous flat format, with no namespacing against a future real option literally named `disabled`. This is a new, permanent piece of public configuration surface for a widely-used linter — worth confirming with maintainers whether a more explicit/structured syntax (e.g. a dedicated `disabled-checks` option) is preferred over this convention before locking it in.
